transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thanks for seeing me. Um… I guess what finally made me book the appointment is this thing where I keep getting up when I’m supposed to stay seated—like during sprint planning at work, or even mortgage calls. It’s not like I’m trying to be rude or anything, I’ll just suddenly feel like I need water, or I’ll decide I should check something in the other room. And I know I should just stay put, but… I don’t always. I’m not sure if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but it’s been happening enough that I thought I should ask.
Thinking back, did you have similar trouble sitting still, staying focused, or feeling restless when you were a child, say in elementary or middle school?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I did fine in school overall, so I don’t want to make it sound like I was constantly in trouble. But I do remember teachers moving my desk sometimes, or reminding me to stay seated because I’d be popping up a lot.

And I guess I also had a habit of talking before I was called on, or rushing through assignments even when I understood the work. It wasn’t meant to be disruptive, at least I don’t think so… but yeah, looking back, there were definitely comments like that.
Aside from the restlessness and impulsivity, have you ever had ongoing problems with things like defying authority, getting into fights, or breaking rules—either as a child or now as an adult?

No, I don’t think so. I mean, I wasn’t… like, a rebellious kid or someone who got into fights. I might’ve been annoying in class sometimes, I’m sure, but not defiant on purpose.

As an adult, same thing—I try pretty hard to follow rules and not cause problems. I don’t think there’s anything like that, unless I’m misunderstanding what you mean.

Do you notice these same difficulties—like restlessness, impulsivity, or trouble focusing—showing up in other areas of your life too, like at home or in social situations, and would you say they've caused real problems for you there?

Yeah… I think it does, although I keep wanting to say it’s not, like, catastrophic or anything. But it has started causing some friction.

At work, people have to follow up with me more than they used to, especially around planning tasks, and that feels… embarrassing. I’m trying really hard, but I worry I’m becoming the unreliable one, which is not how I want to be seen.

And at home it’s similar, just in a smaller way—more reminders, more checking in with me. I don’t know if that counts as a “real problem,” but it’s definitely affecting things more than I’d like.
Do you often find yourself losing focus during tasks, forgetting important things, or misplacing items you need, even when you're trying to pay attention?

Yeah… I mean, not all the time, but it does happen more than I’d like.

Like, I can sit down to review a pull request or read through mortgage documents with every intention of focusing, and then a few minutes later I realize I’ve been staring at the same paragraph or section and my mind is off thinking about five totally unrelated things.

I try to catch myself and come back to it, so I don’t know if that’s the kind of thing you mean, but… yeah, that happens.
Since childhood, have these symptoms been continuously present throughout your life, or was there a stretch—like during college or early adulthood—when they mostly went away before coming back?

I don’t think it ever fully went away, honestly. I might have gotten better at covering for it, especially as I got older, but looking back it was there pretty early.

I remember in elementary school teachers moving my desk or reminding me to stay seated because I was always popping up or talking before I was called on. And I’d rush through things even when I understood the work, which… I guess sounded like carelessness, but I wasn’t trying to be difficult.

So, yeah, I’d say it’s been pretty continuous, just maybe looked different at different ages. Does that make sense?
Have you been experiencing any ongoing anxiety, low mood, or using substances like caffeine, alcohol, or other drugs regularly that might be contributing to your restlessness or trouble focusing?

I don’t think so… at least, nothing obvious comes to mind.

I mean, I have normal stress, like work and life stuff, but I wouldn’t say I’m constantly anxious or depressed. And I’m not using drugs or anything like that. Caffeine is maybe just… normal? Coffee, mostly. I don’t think it explains it, but I guess I’m not totally sure what amount would count as contributing.

Alcohol isn’t a big thing for me either. So… I don’t think there’s a separate thing driving it, but I’m open to being wrong if there’s something specific you’re looking for.
Can you recall whether these behaviors—popping up, talking out of turn, rushing through work—were already noticeable before you turned 12 years old?

Yes, I think so. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it was, because I wasn’t, like, constantly in trouble or anything… but yes, elementary school was definitely before 12.

I remember teachers moving my desk sometimes, or reminding me to stay seated because I’d pop up a lot. And I’d talk before I was called on, or rush through work even when I actually understood it. So… yeah, those things were noticeable pretty early, I think.
